label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Subject: Re: Our plan for next year**

Dear Appa, Amma, Kiran, Divya and all,

Sorry for the slow reply. I've just come off a run of nights and only properly sat down with everyone's messages today.

First, I'm so happy you're both coming. I keep picturing Amma in the kitchen and Appa out at the back, and I'm a bit emotional about it. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable for the fridge. It includes "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays," so Amma, I'm afraid you've been booked.

Kiran, you're right, and I want to say that clearly. You should have heard about this from me much earlier, and certainly before any paperwork started. The visa agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, so I got on with that part and didn't stop to pick up the phone to you. That was my mistake. I'm sorry you found out the way you did. It wasn't a long secret plan between me and Amma and Appa. Appa first mentioned it in August, when Rohan was showing him our vegetable patch on a video call and Appa said, "I could grow drumsticks there." Things moved quickly after that, and I should have brought you in right then.

Your concerns are fair, and I've thought about all three, so here's where things stand.

**1. Appa's heart.** This is the one I've thought about most, and you're right that visitors aren't covered by the NHS for most hospital care. I've got a quote for travel insurance that specifically includes pre-existing cardiac conditions. It's about £640 each for the six months, and the agent has confirmed it covers the stent. I'll send you the policy wording so you can read it yourself. Dr. Prakash has agreed to do Appa's full review in March, before they fly, and a video consult in July while they're here. He's happy to share his notes with me, so he stays Appa's doctor throughout and nothing gets lost between Bangalore and here. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from our house, and I know a lot of the cardiology team there, so if anything did happen, Appa would be in good hands quickly. The annexe at the back is finished too. It's all on the ground floor with no steps, and it has its own shower with a grab rail.

**2. Amma and the six months.** This is a really good point and I hadn't thought about it the way you put it. Six months is long, and Amma hasn't been away from home that long in years. The return ticket is flexible, so if she's homesick or just wants her own house and her own people, she can go back whenever she likes, with no fuss and no guilt. Amma, please hold me to that. The plan only works if it's good for you.

**3. Ganesh Chaturthi in Pune.** I don't want this to take that away from you and Divya. I can see two ways to keep it. One is that Amma and Appa fly from here to Pune in September for Ganesh Chaturthi and end their trip with you, then go home to Bangalore from there. The other is that all of you come to Leicester in August, in which case I'd like to cover your flights. I really mean it, please let me. Either way, the kids get time with their cousins and with Paati and Thatha, and Pune still gets them for the festival or close to it.

You're also right that this needs a proper conversation, not just emails. Can we all get on a video call this Sunday, 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? Appa and Amma can tell us what they're hoping for, and Kiran, I'd really like to hear what else is on your mind, because I'm sure there's more than fits in an email. Nothing is set in stone beyond the visa application, and that doesn't go in until January.

Divya, I'll make sure the murukku achu makes it into the suitcase, even if it has to sit next to the pickles.

Love to all of you,
Meera
